title: Label provenance & dedupe heuristics (scratch)
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for provenance-aware de-duplication rules and label resolution heuristics. Goal is to reduce false duplicates, preserve high-quality human labels, and create a transparent tie-break order when the same or near-duplicate examples carry conflicting labels from different sources.

Context notes (why we need this):
- We've seen a lot of collision cases where vendor uploads + automated ingestion + user-submissions all exist for the same semantic example (often paraphrases or noisy transcriptions).
- Naive exact-string dedupe throws away curated human labels. Fuzzy dedupe that uses only textual similarity can collapse distinct intents (e.g., "cancel my subscription" vs "how do I cancel?" sometimes treated the same but label sets differ).
- We need a small, auditable set of heuristics that:
  1) flags likely duplicates for automated merging or review,
  2) chooses a label provenance priority, and
  3) provides a human-in-the-loop path for ambiguous conflicts.

High-level provenance priority (proposal):
1) internal-curated (senior annotator / review team)
2) internal-labeler (full-time labeler with >X hours on our tasks)
3) vendor-curated (trusted vendor batches, annotated by humans)
4) automated-inference (auto-labeled via model distillation / weak supervision)
5) external-user-submission (end-user or partner uploads)

Rationale: curated internal sets most trusted; vendor above automated because human-in-the-loop usually better; external-user-submissions lowest because often noisy / duplicate. This is configurable per dataset - some customer datasets should reverse priorities (customer labels are authoritative).

Deduplication signals (ordered):
- exact-normalized-string match: after whitespace collapse, unicode normalization (NFC), and basic punctuation strip (.,!?;:)
- normalized-lowercase + canonicalized entities: substitute emails/urls/numbers with tokens (<EMAIL>, <URL>, <NUM>)
- edit-distance threshold (levenshtein) for short strings (< 64 chars): threshold = 0.15 * length
- token-based Jaccard / overlap for longer samples
- embedding cosine similarity (SBERT or in-house encoder) > 0.92 => candidate duplicate; treat with caution if token overlap low
- fuzzy-hash / simhash fingerprint match (for paraphrase heavy corpora)

Suggested multi-stage pipeline:
Stage A: fast pre-filter (cheap ops)
- apply normalization (case, unicode, drop diacritics optionally)
- exact tokenized equality -> mark as duplicate (auto-merge if same provenance priority)
- simhash binning -> candidate pairs

Stage B: secondary scoring (slower ops)
- compute token-levenshtein and token-overlap
- compute embedding cosine (approx nearest neighbors using faiss index)
- combine into composite score: score = max(embedding_sim, 1 - norm_edit_distance, token_overlap)
- threshold rules:
  * if score > 0.96 and provenance is non-conflicting -> auto-merge
  * if 0.92 < score <= 0.96 and labels match -> auto-merge with provenance tag list
  * if score > 0.92 and labels conflict -> send to conflict queue (HITL)

Label conflict resolution rules (when same sample has different labels):
- If provenance priority differs -> pick higher priority label, attach provenance history (do not delete lower-priority label, store as alternate)
- If same priority but labeler agreement < 0.6 across N labelers -> escalate to review pool
- If label type is continuous / score -> average weighted by labeler quality score
- For categorical labels with tie -> random tie-breaker discouraged; prefer review or pick label with higher historical accuracy on a calibration set

Retention & auditing:
- Keep provenance chain for every retained example in metadata: created_by, source, original_id, upload_batch, labeler_id(s), label_timestamps, merge_actions (timestamp + by whom + rule used)
- Expose small human-readable summary: "was merged from 3 duplicates; chosen label: vendor-curated; alternate labels preserved"

Edge cases and examples (concrete):
1) ASR transcripts: multiple transcriptions of same audio (punct variation, filler words). Rule: prefer human transcript > auto-transcript; if embedding sim > 0.95 consider same sample; store audio_id pointer and unify via audio_id rather than text.
2) Email/URL heavy samples: normalization must mask tokens, but remember original text in metadata. Two samples differing only in email should be considered duplicates.
3) Long documents vs. snippets: when a snippet appears inside a long doc, flag as "contained" not "duplicate"; allow both to coexist unless label mapping suggests they truly correspond.
4) Paraphrase with different intent labels: if embedding sim high but label semantics differ (intent vs sentiment), do NOT auto-merge; add rule to compare label types.

Labeler quality and weighting (notes):
- Maintain rolling accuracy estimates per labeler from calibration tasks (gold set). Use this for weighted label voting and for trust thresholds to bypass manual review.
- Vendor labelers get a group score; individual vendor annotators not tracked unless required by contract.

Human-in-loop UI expectations (what I want from Relabeling tool):
- show the top 5 candidate duplicates sorted by composite score
- display provenance chain and prior labels with timestamps
- quick actions: accept merge, create canonical example, keep both, re-label, add to gold set
- allow bulk accept if rule applied to entire batch (audit log required)

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to handle temporal drift? two identical queries months apart may expect different labels (policy change). Need "policy effective date" in provenance.
- Tune embedding threshold per dataset: general threshold 0.92 is noisy; run sampling experiments per customer.
- Add confidence heuristics when labels come from models (include model version + eval metrics)
- Policy for deleting duplicates: soft-delete with retention 90 days before purge; add admin flag to bypass purge for enterprise customers.

Quick experiments to run next week:
- sample 10k candidate duplicate pairs (embedding sim 0.9-0.95) and have triage team label whether they are true duplicates; compute precision/recall at different thresholds
- A/B test priority ordering for one customer where external-user-submission should be authoritative (flip priority and measure label disagreement rate)

Notes-to-self (loose):
- talk to Mateo about adding model-version metadata in upstream ingestion (ticket ML-4572)
- ask SRE if we can add simhash prefilter to ingestion pipeline (cost implications)
- create small confluence page documenting final heuristics and the "why" (link above)

Examples (for experimentation):
- "I want to cancel my plan" vs "how do I cancel my subscription?" -> embedding_sim: 0.88, token overlap moderate -> probably same intent but check label set
- "Reset password" vs "forgot password email" -> likely duplicates for intent-routing training; treat as duplicates if labels identical
- "Order status #12345" vs "where is my order 12345" -> mask numbers -> duplicate

End of scratch. This is a working doc — throwaway until we land on rules. Keep this under users/ for now; once stable, move to shared_drives/product or confluence.
